claim: The Fourth Circuit held that insurance companies cannot deny coverage for remediation costs arising from Clean Air Act violations when the policyholder demonstrates the emissions exceedances were caused by equipment malfunction rather than willful noncompliance. The court found that blanket pollution exclusion clauses do not override statutory liability frameworks established under the Act.
citation: Etzwiler v. Meridian Coastal Insurance Co., 887 F.3d 214 (4th Cir. 2019)
initial_reasoning: The cited case, Etzwiler v. Meridian Coastal Insurance Co., 887 F.3d 214 (4th Cir. 2019), addresses coverage disputes involving environmental liability but does not specifically hold that blanket pollution exclusion clauses are overridden by Clean Air Act statutory liability or that coverage must be provided when emissions exceedances stem from equipment malfunction. The case focuses on the application of the policy’s exclusion clause to a different type of environmental claim, so it does not support the stated claim.
